seams.transport: runtime-only PreparedSession beside CohortSession: RowJob carries prepared_root + residency cap; worker process constructs the session once per root, attaches as una._prepared_session; session detached before RowResult transport and state-bundle packing (cohort precedent batch/worker.py:347-411)
seams.resolution_constraint: Topology._apply_stage_cache_policy (Topology.py:188-193) refreshes cache_options from settings at EVERY Add* head — a session cannot inject CacheOptions once. WORSE, topology.cache_options is ALSO read by the engine's RESULT stage (AccessibilityWElevation.py:930-931, Accessibility.py:842 resolve _stage_cache_for(getattr(topology,'cache_options',None)) for the una:awe:o_access:v1 results stage) — so injecting the session's store through cache_options would silently enable results caching, which P02 forbids. The seam is therefore a SEPARATE resolver attribute on Topology (e.g. _prepared_stage_cache) consulted ONLY at the two Add* preparation call sites (Topology.py:226, 1013): session attached AND stage admitted -> the session's StageCache; otherwise the existing expression evaluated on the row's own cache_options. topology.cache_options itself is never touched by the session; the result stage keeps reading exactly what the row's settings say (off for the frozen policy)

hook_points.AddNetwork: after the isfile gate (210-211), before decode (254): consult session for una:topology:v1; hit -> _restore_network_from_cache; miss -> arrays_once single-flight around (decode + BuildTopology + store)
hook_points.AddOrigins/AddDestinations: after the isfile gate, inside BuildAccessPoints's existing cache block position (1013-1034): hit -> _restore_access_points_from_cache; miss -> single-flight around (decode + validation + weights + snap + store)
hook_points.validation_order: geometry/CRS/weights validation happens INSIDE the miss/owner path exactly as today; a hit skips only the re-derivation, never the row's own isfile/Validation gates

seams.no_public_api_change: RunAccessibility's statement order unchanged; serial route and session-less runs take today's code; unadmitted inputs keep the existing route (design line 13)

state_machine.primitive: cache.stages.StageCache.arrays_once (stages.py:140-187): cross-process store.singleflight per key; owner produces once and commits; losers re-get; >=3 unproductive spins or wait timeout -> local compute; StageProduced marker distinguishes owner compute from hit (review MAJOR-1 law)
state_machine.owner_failure: exception inside the flight leaves no commit; waiters re-elect or compute locally; a failed producer never suppresses waiters' own validation/errors
state_machine.cancellation: owner cancellation discards incomplete bytes (store crash/partial laws: tests/cache/store/test_corruption_crash_partial.py); no partial acceptance

counters_law.attribution: CohortSession mark/delta pattern (cohort.py:199-235); per-row slice rides RowResult; aggregate reported through the batch report under the run-scoped session
counters_law.engagement_asserts: counts are asserted in tests (P00 precedent: singleflight_lost 31/31, zero refusals)

memory_law.admission_reservation: build scratch + retained payload + decoded worker copies + current row + receiver bytes reserved BEFORE build admission
memory_law.residency_sizing: ENFORCED law (C31-MINOR-1): per-worker cap max(64 MiB, allowance//workers); floor-bound caps may sum to 64 MiB x workers (documented exception, unit-pinned)
memory_law.no_fit: explicit pre-execution refusal counted as refusal; never a silent fallback inside a cap claim
memory_law.registry_bound: design line 121: the per-process store registry must be bounded (cohort's _PROCESS_STORES is an unbounded per-root registry — the prepared session does not add a second unbounded one)
memory_law.no_native_transport: GDALDataset/GEOS/STRtree/open handles never cross processes; edge_sindex is derived state rebuilt per restore (Topology.py:400-403)

fallback_and_failure_order.law: any refusal -> the row takes the CURRENT path with zero observable difference; refusals counted
refusal_taxonomy: payload not representable (mixed-dim WKB, uid dtype outside ifubU)
row_gates_never_skipped: skip-gate and error observation per row
fallback_and_failure_order.error_attachment: a preparation failure attaches to the logical row/stage original execution would fail; no eager preparation of future rows ahead of earlier commits (design lines 36-38)

must_miss: network bytes change -> topology + both snaps + results
origins/destinations/obstacles bytes change -> that snap + results
network_precision / weight column / semantic_profile change -> all five
obstacle snap_to/direction/penalty-column change -> as pinned per stage
must_hit: output-only changes (folder, file name, wStamp, delimiter, format flags) reuse all preparation stages (test_output_only_changes_reuse.py)
invalidation_matrix.freshness: hit payloads are fresh copies per restore; mutating a restored payload cannot poison later runs (test_parity_safety_engagement.py:74)

restore_fidelity_law.crs: PROJJSON round-trip only (WKT datum-ensemble loss is an observed artifact-hash delta, Topology.py:363-366); restored crs must equal uncached crs (pinned test)
restore_fidelity_law.geometry: WKB byte_order=1, output_dimension=coord_dim; mixed-dimension layers are a skip (miss), never a truncation
restore_fidelity_law.uid: Series-ness and dtype preserved within the ifubU law; object/void dtypes refuse storage (miss)
restore_fidelity_law.derived_state: edge_sindex rebuilt from restored geometries (same order/bits); never stored, never shared
restore_fidelity_law.logs: content-derived v<=2 lines replayed through the row's own logger (audit section 10); hit announcement v2
restore_fidelity_law.bitwise_gate: warm(restored) vs cold(off) artifacts bitwise equal on the public entry point (pinned test) — the P02 equivalent must hold on the RunBatch public surface

increments.A: reader/state equivalence + store/restore fixtures on the admitted domain; no dispatch change (mostly exists: CACHE_GRAPH suites; add .feather/.parquet parity fixtures if absent)
increments.B: worker-local prepared reuse across rows within one worker process (at most W first builds); low-risk ablation
increments.C: run-wide content single-flight across worker processes: one decode/build per stable identity plus at most W geometry/STRtree reconstructions; move no work outside RunBatch; count actual preparations, not only trace hits
increments.D: engine-payload reuse ONLY if measured cost justifies; excluded by default

non_goals: no public CacheOptions semantics change; the frozen cache-off primary remains untouched
no persistent cross-run cache introduced by the prepared session (run-scoped root beside row outputs; content-addressed; produce-once within the run; residency-governed)
no turn/elevation-derivation, obstacle, flow, or results-stage reuse in v1
no double counting with P01 relief: preparation relief is per-row stretch relief on the workers' critical resource (P01M H1 verdict), never idle relief
no new speedup claimed by this document; acceptance requires measured public benefit (design line 134)

resolved_determinations.admitted_formats: geojson-only for v1 — the parity/invalidation suites build geojson INPUTS exclusively (conftest.py:80-112); feather/parquet appear only as OUTPUT formats. Format admission widens only with increment-A fixtures
resolved_determinations.loser_path_under_owner_crash: SATISFIES the design law: produce() AND commit run while holding the per-key flight (stages.py:173-177), so a crashed owner leaves no commit; the loser re-gets None, and after >=3 unproductive spins computes locally (stages.py:178-184) — the design's 'original compute path'. A late second publisher can only emit an identical generation (key closure pins all numerical inputs, stages.py:158-162). Partial-write residue is covered by the store's corruption laws (no hit from corrupt bytes, test_corruption_crash_partial.py)
resolved_determinations.cohort_stage_key_consistency: CONSISTENT (as amended by BF-1): a stage key is a pure closure hash (cache/identity.py:135-140) — it encodes no store root or store identity. The run-scoped store serves entries under keys that MAY carry extra disambiguation components (BF-1: the snap store key adds 'role'); the restored object's OBSERVED _stage_key must equal the CACHE_GRAPH closure value (role-free for snap) so every stage-key read (AccessibilityWElevation.py:854-856 result-key composition) sees exactly the value the current CACHE_GRAPH machinery computes. Design line 62 sanctions the split: a locator is not identity. The resolver therefore computes TWO hashes for a snap stage: store_key = stage_key('una:snap:v1', {closure + role}), stage_key_observed = stage_key('una:snap:v1', {closure}); the topology stage keeps store_key == stage_key_observed (single role, no ambiguity)

does the B-then-C increment ordering leave any window where worker-local reuse and run-wide single-flight interact to produce more than one decode per identity per run (the design caps: one build per identity, at most W reconstructions)?
